IEE Colloquium on Activate Human Resources and Transform Your Business (Digest No. 1998/418)
abstract: As companies have repeatedly downsized it should not come as a surprise that concern about job security has grown, particularly in organisations where problem solving and improvement groups operate. The feeling that by helping to improve productivity and efficiency employees are cutting their own throats is beginning to emerge quite strongly. We have to find ways to counteract these feelings through redeployment, retraining and, where appropriate, through security agreements of the type recently pioneered by United Distillers and Blue Circle.

articleTitle: Using the business excellence model to transform your business
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Activate Human Resources and Transform Your Business (Digest No. 1998/418)
abstract: The key to business success is all about people. Any organisation is only as good as its people. In essence, business excellence stems not so much from the management of total quality, as far too many people still perceive, but from the total quality of management in all its guises. The latter practice subsumes the former but involves much more. This paper briefly covers the underlying reason for the creation of the European business excellence model, its components and how it is increasingly being used to complement other approaches to activate people to transform their business.

articleTitle: People: the competitive edge or the weak link in the chain?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Activate Human Resources and Transform Your Business (Digest No. 1998/418)
abstract: Maintaining employee perceptions that management is operating in good faith with employees, having their best interests in mind and maintaining the best possible balance between the interests of customers, investors and employees will become increasingly important. 'Trust, fairness and the delivery of the deal' are the basis for the psychological contract. Given this we may be able to achieve performance improvements that have somehow always seemed to be well beyond management's grasp - to get and keep the competitive edge we have been looking for. People may turn out to be the weak link in the performance chain but if so the weak link will be one of management's own making.

articleTitle: Making a difference - through the self-actualisation of the individual
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Activate Human Resources and Transform Your Business (Digest No. 1998/418)
abstract: At the heart of change processes are people. Through leading edge research and working within organisations, the author has developed a fresh approach to activating human resources. It is centred on the self-actualisation of the individual and requires new thinking, new roles and new skills throughout the organisation.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Activate Human Resources and Transform Your Business (Digest No. 1998/418)
abstract: Throughout the 1990s Rover Group has been implementing a major change programme called "success through people". The strategic goal of this programme has been to create a world class learning organisation, where we continuously develop our skills and capabilities, to ensure that we are always able to delight our customers with world beating products. An associate development process was developed to identify our individual and team development needs, so that when we work together in teams, we have the confidence to express our individual creativity and to maximise our involvement and contribution to business performance improvement.
